domain_label: Turlock Independent Retail & Goods — Business Models & Unit Economics
purpose: A method for reasoning about how each independent Retail & Goods format in Turlock and Stanislaus County is actually run as a business — its offering and inventory model, family/owner labor and incumbency, seller's-permit / C-45 / secondhand-dealer licensing gate, equipment capex, cost structure and labeled benchmark margins, supplier chain, and the operating decisions that make a discretionary specialty-retail format viable or doom it — without ever stating a named business's dollar revenue as fact.
assumptions: no observed per-business financials supplied; every dollar band is a labeled industry-benchmark estimate scaled by an observable size signal (format, footprint, incumbency, headcount), tagged estimate-not-actual, never a claim of actual revenue for any named business such as Vail Creek, Camara's Clothier, or Main Street Antiques

the universe is the 27 verified independent Retail & Goods businesses in Turlock catalogued in businesses.json across 12 sub-categories (chains excluded), in a town of ~72,500 with ~8,455 CSU Stanislaus students and a deep ethnic life-event economy; the 27 count is a FLOOR, not a ceiling

city, county, state and demographic figures used here (population, income, ancestry shares, license fees, the C-45 $15k bond) are cited public facts from the deep-dive or labeled derivations, not invented

supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference about the realistic supply universe, not confirmed contracts, unless a cited source states the relationship (Vintage Market's Annie Sloan dealership; Lightly Used Books' March 2025 store closure; Main Street Antiques' 28+-dealer structure)
cost-structure and margin benchmarks are published industry figures (COGS/markup/gross/net) applied as planning priors, not audited operator P&Ls
exclusions: chain, franchise and big-box retail operations (the catalog is independents only)
stating any actual dollar revenue, profit, or owner income for a specifically named Turlock business as fact
demand-and-saturation market sizing as a standalone deliverable beyond what is needed to judge a format's viability (the detail lives in the market/reconciled analyses)
grocery, automotive, health/pharmacy and food-service retail except where a Retail & Goods format straddles into a food/cosmetics arm (e.g. Vintage Market's bath/beauty)
tax, legal, and licensing advice for an individual operator; this models formats and decisions, not a specific filing

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_GO_NOGO composes saturation, cost gate and demand headroom into a defensible add/avoid verdict (no sixth thrift, fourth antiques, or naive second bridal generalist; favor custom-print, sign, and specialized/destination formalwear) each conditioned on clearing the capex and C-45/secondhand gate

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every dollar band in this KB: the figure is a published industry benchmark (revenue per store/per employee, markup ratio, booth-rent norm) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal, never a reported or claimed actual revenue for any named business.

An observable proxy (format, storefront footprint, years of incumbency, headcount, dealer-booth count) used to scale a published per-unit benchmark into a planning revenue band, in place of unavailable actual sales.
The 2x cost-to-retail pricing convention common in apparel, gifts and decor (cost ~50%, gross ~50%); jewelry can run triple-keystone on some lines, dropping COGS toward ~33%.

Donated-goods thrift posts high gross margin on near-zero COGS yet thin net margin, because the squeeze is on the sector's highest sorting labor and foot-traffic-capped low-ticket volume, not on COGS — high gross never means high profit here.

The operator economics of a multi-dealer mall such as Main Street Antiques (28+ dealers): revenue is booth rent plus a ~10-40% sales commission plus 2-4% card fees, not inventory ownership — a landlord-plus-checkout P&L over many micro-inventories.

The CSLB sign-contractor license gating sign installation and electrical/illuminated signs (Posted, J & J): requires 4 years journeyman experience, an exam, and a $15,000 contractor bond — the single hardest licensing gate in the sector.
The jewelry-trade practice of holding wholesaler diamonds/gems on memo (consignment) rather than buying them outright, which reduces upfront cash tied up in high-value, low-turnover stock.

Turlock's unusually deep ethnic life-event calendar — Assyrian and Portuguese weddings and festivals, Mexican quinceaneras and sacraments, Sikh ceremonies — that drives repeat demand for formalwear, florals, gold jewelry and custom print at counts a same-size generic town could not sustain.

The demand cap created by Modesto's Vintage Faire Mall and big-box/chain retail (15 minutes north), Amazon, and online resale (Poshmark/ThredUp/eBay) siphoning mid-tier apparel, gift, book and commodity spend out of Turlock — the largest single force capping the independent count.

The discipline that the 27-business catalog is a curated independents-only floor, not a ceiling: home-based sellers, the 28+ booth dealers inside Main Street Antiques, pop-ups and newer entrants are under-captured, so ~3.7/10k density and every white-space read is a lower bound.

nodes.definition: Establish the discretionary-spend floor every Turlock Retail & Goods format draws on: ~72,500 residents at a median household income of ~$82,995 across ~25,365 households, a median age ~35, and ~8,455 CSU Stanislaus students whose term-time presence lifts boutique and gift demand. This is a solidly middle-income but cost-conscious Central Valley base well below coastal California, so price sensitivity is high for everyday apparel, gifts and books and low only for the irreplaceable event purchase. Unlike Food & Dining, the sector is ~100% discretionary with no necessity floor and no third-party-payer buffer, so its demand is cyclically geared to consumer confidence. This is the size of the pie before any format question is asked.

included: resident population, income and household count
CSU Stanislaus student demand
the 100%-discretionary, no-payer-buffer nature of the sector
high price sensitivity except for event purchases

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a population, income, or enrollment figure is updated

pros.claim: Sizing the base from cited public figures grounds every format judgment in real local discretionary income instead of national noise
pros.example: the ~$82,995 median across ~25,365 households sets a cost-conscious ceiling that caps how many boutiques and gift shops the trade area can feed

cons.claim: A middling income figure invites under-reading event-defended categories whose demand is cultural, not income-led
cons.example: treating gold jewelry or bridal demand as income-capped when the ethnic life-event calendar drives it

ignoring the term-time swing of student demand and over-building for a 12-month calendar

nodes.definition: Tie Turlock's unusual heritage depth to the specific Retail & Goods formats it sustains. The town holds an Assyrian community estimated near ~20,000 (~a quarter of the city; magnitude is an estimate, not a Census fact), a ~7% Portuguese/Azorean ancestry, a ~46% Hispanic majority that is overwhelmingly Mexican-origin, and a notable Punjabi/Sikh presence. These communities run culture-heavy life-event calendars — Assyrian and Portuguese weddings and festivals, Mexican quinceaneras and sacraments, Sikh ceremonies — that drive repeat demand for formalwear, florals, jewelry (gold gifting is central to South-Asian and Hispanic tradition) and custom-print/embroidery. This is precisely why one bridal store, three jewelers, three florists and a custom-apparel shop survive at counts a same-size Midwest town could not, and it is the load-bearing reason the independent count does not collapse lower.

included: Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican and Punjabi/Sikh shares with sources and estimate labels
the format each community anchors
the strongest-event-calendar driver behind survival
excluded: the cost structure of each format

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a heritage community's size or the format it anchors changes

pros.claim: Mapping the life-event calendar to formats explains both why a format exists and how durable its demand is
pros.example: the ethnic-wedding and quinceanera economy makes one bridal store, three florists and three jewelers well-matched rather than over-built

cons.claim: Event demand is culturally durable but capped by the annual number of weddings/funerals, not by store count, so it can be mistaken for a growth lane
cons.example: treating a fixed annual wedding pool as expandable because the Hispanic and Assyrian bases are large

failure_modes: assuming a large community implies unlimited format headroom
stating the ~20k Assyrian figure as a Census fact when it is a community/press estimate
acceptance_tests: each heritage community is given its cited or estimate-labeled share and the specific format(s) it anchors, distinguishing durable from growing demand and tagging the ~20k figure an estimate
revisit_triggers: ancestry shares shift in a Census refresh
a heritage community grows or contracts via migration

nodes.definition: Account for the single biggest cap on Turlock retail demand: leakage. Modesto (~15 minutes north) with Vintage Faire Mall and big-box/department/chain-jewelry retail captures most mid-tier apparel, gift and brand-jewelry browsing; Amazon pulls commodity gifts, books and basic apparel (the force that pushed Lightly Used Books offline in March 2025); online resale (Poshmark/ThredUp/eBay) competes directly with the crowded thrift cluster; and Bay Area/Monterey outlets and national bridal/jewelry e-tail pressure the premium and high-consideration categories. Any format judgment that ignores this leakage over-states Turlock headroom — especially for cross-shopped, commodity formats (gifts, basic apparel, books) as opposed to event-defended local-service ones (bridal, fine jewelry, sympathy florals) whose fit-and-service moat resists it.

included: Modesto/Vintage Faire, Amazon, online-resale and outlet/e-tail leakage channels
which spend categories leak
which formats are most vs least exposed
excluded: the measured leakage figure (it is a behavioral estimate, not a count)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: regional retail supply in Modesto or online share shifts

pros.claim: Naming the leakage channels explains why population alone over-predicts Turlock's specialty-retail count
pros.example: commodity gift and book demand leaks to Amazon, which is why the used-bookstore went online-only and the gift singleton is hazardous rather than inviting

cons.claim: The leakage is an estimate of cross-shopping behavior, not a measured figure, so it can be over- or under-applied
cons.example: assuming all discretionary spend leaks when downtown Turlock retains a loyal event and destination base

failure_modes: applying the ceiling uniformly to event-defended local-service formats that do not cross-shop
treating the leakage as measured when it is a behavioral estimate
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the Modesto/Amazon/resale/outlet channels and ranks formats by exposure to leakage, flagging the figure as a behavioral estimate
revisit_triggers: a major retail development opens in Modesto or Turlock
an online-retail share shift re-rates a commodity category
a cross-shop leakage study is produced

nodes.definition: Define the binding honesty discipline that governs every number in this KB, because per-business revenue is not public for these privately held independents. No dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business; every revenue, margin or market-size number is a labeled benchmark estimate — a published industry benchmark scaled by an observable size signal — that explicitly carries the word estimate, a method, a public source anchor and a confidence level, and the method + source + confidence must travel with the number wherever it goes. City/county figures (population, income, the C-45 $15k bond, license fees) are cited public facts or labeled derivations; supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference unless the catalog documents them; and coverage is reported as a FLOOR, not a ceiling. High gross is always paired with the thin-net caveat so it is never mistaken for profit.

included: the estimate-not-actual label with method + source + confidence
the cited-fact vs inference vs floor distinctions
the high-gross-paired-with-thin-net rule
excluded: the specific revenue bands themselves (those live in the format nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the availability of actual per-business data or a documentable supplier link changes

pros.claim: Making the label a first-class node stops any band from circulating as a private business's actual revenue
pros.example: a jewelry band of $350k-$900k carried with its national-benchmark method, source and medium confidence rather than attributed to Vail Creek

cons.claim: The discipline is verbose and can be dropped under pressure to give a single clean number
cons.example: a stakeholder asking for one revenue figure for a named store and the label being stripped to satisfy them

failure_modes: presenting a benchmark band as a fact for a named business
upgrading a representative supplier link to a stated contract
reading the 27-count as a ceiling rather than a floor
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure produced carries the word estimate, a method, a public source anchor and a confidence level, no named business's revenue is stated as fact, and coverage is flagged as a floor
revisit_triggers: a source providing actual per-business revenue becomes available
a supplier contract is documented and can be upgraded from inference
the catalog floor is expanded with newly found entrants

nodes.definition: Lay down the published, cited cost-structure backbone every format model is read against: apparel COGS ~45-50% (keystone 2x, gross ~50-55%); gifts/decor keystone 2x (~50% gross); jewelry keystone ~50% to triple-keystone ~33% COGS (gross ~50-67%); florist floral COGS ~30-45% with design+delivery labor ~20-30%; custom apparel/print blanks ~25-40% with high operator labor (gross ~60-75%); sign/print substrate ~20-35% with capex depreciation (gross ~65-80%); thrift near-0% COGS on donations to ~40-60% on consignor splits; antique-mall operator earns booth rent + ~10-40% commission + 2-4% card fees. Cross-sector: independent-retail net margin ~3-13%, occupancy/rent ~5-15% of revenue, payroll ~10-20%. These are planning benchmark estimates keyed to Shopify/Toast/NRF and trade data, not audited Turlock P&Ls, and they are the lens that turns a revenue band into a margin reality.

cons.claim: Published benchmarks lag and average away the family-labor and incumbency advantages that move real Turlock margins, and no Turlock rent figure is sourced
cons.example: the payroll benchmark overstates cost for an owner-operated jeweler using unpaid family bench labor

nodes.definition: Define the only honest way to attach a revenue band to a format when no per-business revenue is public: take a published industry benchmark (US florist avg ~$385k-$685k; independent jeweler typical B&M ~$0.9-1.0M; bridal ~2.5-3x markup at avg gown ~$1,900; signage franchise avg ~$667k; custom screen-print startups ~$100k-$200k) and scale it DOWN by an observable Turlock size signal (format, footprint, incumbency, headcount) to reflect below-coastal income and small-market size, then tag the result estimate-not-actual, assign a confidence level (uniformly Low-Med since no Turlock-specific data exists), and name the confirmation path (CDTFA / Turlock Finance sales-tax receipts). The per-sub-category bands run florist $180k-$450k, jewelry $350k-$900k, bridal $300k-$900k, custom print $120k-$600k, sign $200k-$700k, antiques $80k-$400k, thrift $60k-$300k, bookstore $30k-$150k — deliberately wide, never a point figure for a named store.

included: benchmark-times-size-signal scaled-down method
the estimate-not-actual label, Low-Med confidence and confirmation path
the per-sub-category bands as ranges not points
excluded: stating a named business's actual revenue

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark, a size signal, or the availability of confirming sales-tax data changes

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band gives a defensible planning number without ever claiming a private business's actual revenue
pros.example: a small delivery-leaning florist scaled below the US ~$385k-$685k average to a $180k-$450k band tagged estimate with a sales-tax confirmation path

cons.claim: A benchmark band can be over-trusted if the size signal is mis-observed or the confidence label is dropped
cons.example: treating a footprint-based estimate as precise when the store's actual turns and ticket are unknown

failure_modes: dropping the estimate-not-actual label and presenting a band as a fact
scaling from a luxury-metro benchmark without discounting for Turlock's below-coastal income
acceptance_tests: every revenue band produced carries the estimate-not-actual label, a Low-Med confidence, the size signal used, and a named confirmation source, and is presented as a range scaled down from a cited national benchmark
revisit_triggers: a published per-store/per-employee benchmark is updated

a format's observable size signal changes

nodes.definition: Explain the swing variables that let Turlock's thin-margin discretionary independents survive: owner/family labor paid below market or not at all, and deep incumbency. Family labor suppresses the published ~10-20% retail payroll benchmark, while decades of incumbency lower occupancy risk (often owned or long-held space), build a defended local-service reputation, and amortize fixtures — the reason heritage names endure: J & J Printing since 1975, Camara's Clothier 40+ years, Glitz since 2005, Flowers By Eva 25+ years, Vail Creek 22+ years, and Yonan's Jewelers as Turlock's oldest family-owned jeweler across three generations (the recurring Assyrian family-business density). The lever has hard limits: it caps growth at the family's capacity, masks the true cost of labor when planning a sale, and breaks at succession or burnout — and a generalist new entrant without incumbency cannot replicate it.

the named heritage incumbents
the succession/burnout/scaling limits and the entrant disadvantage

nodes.definition: Establish the baseline licensing every Retail & Goods business must clear: a CDTFA California seller's permit (sales tax) is required of every retailer/wholesaler selling tangible goods and applies to all 27 — and it is free to obtain — plus a City of Turlock business license and a downtown zoning/use permit. This is the sector's defining regulatory fact: the barrier to entry is low, so demand and capital, not licensing, are the real cap for most formats. The permit floor is cheap and fast relative to the C-45 bond, the secondhand-dealer registration and the capex gates that bind only narrow slices, but it is mandatory and the use-permit step is where downtown storefront occupancy is cleared before opening.

nodes.definition: Define the hardest licensing gate in the sector. The CSLB C-45 Sign Contractor license gates sign installation and electrical/illuminated signage (Posted; J & J for installed/illuminated work): it requires 4 years of journeyman experience, an exam, and a $15,000 contractor bond, and California city sign permits typically must be pulled by a licensed C-45 contractor. A related CSLB contractor license may apply to custom-furniture install/build once a job exceeds the ~$500 labor-and-materials threshold (relevant to D2, Rustic Roots), though in-shop sale of finished pieces generally does not trigger it. This skilled-labor-plus-bond moat — alongside the capex stack — is exactly why the operationally hard sign/print white space stays thin even where B2B demand exists: few operators can clear the C-45 barrier.

included: the C-45 4-year/exam/$15k-bond requirement for sign install
the ~$500-threshold contractor rule for custom-furniture install
why the gate keeps sign white space thin

cons.claim: The contractor-license threshold for furniture install is a CSLB-rule estimate whose bite depends on the specific job

acceptance_tests: the C-45 experience/exam/$15k-bond requirement and the ~$500 furniture-install threshold are stated with sources, and the C-45 is identified as the binding gate keeping sign white space thin

nodes.definition: Model the multi-dealer antique mall, a landlord economic hiding inside the Antiques category: Main Street Antiques (28+ dealers) is one destination, not four rivals, and its operator P&L is landlord-plus-checkout, not inventory ownership. conflict_axes.name: heritage_event_depth_vs_leakage_cap
conflict_axes.description: Heritage event demand raises the viable format count while Modesto and online leakage cap it; a format read can over-weight either force.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply event depth to local-service event-defended formats and the leakage cap to commodity cross-shopped ones

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_cost_gate
conflict_axes.description: A format with real demand headroom may still be cost-gated by the C-45 bond, secondhand registration or capex, so demand-true is not the same as enterable.
poles: enter only where the cost gate clears
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true but cost-gated white space as a no-go until the binding gate is cleared

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: High-gross formats (thrift on donations, jewelry on keystone, sign/print on substrate) can post strong gross while netting thin once labor, sorting, insurance and capex service are loaded.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the gross with its net, sorting/labor and capex-service load before judging attractiveness

conflict_axes.name: family_incumbency_survival_vs_scalability
conflict_axes.description: Owner/family labor and incumbency let a thin-margin format survive but cap growth, break at succession, and cannot be replicated by a generalist entrant.
poles: lean on family labor and incumbency to survive
hire out and pay market rent to scale or enter
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use family labor and owned space to clear thin margins but model hired-labor and market-rent cost before assuming growth, a sale, or new-entrant viability

conflict_axes.name: event_durability_vs_fixed_pool_share_split
conflict_axes.description: A culturally durable event format (bridal, jewelry, florals) has defended demand, but the annual event pool is fixed, so a naive second store splits share rather than growing the market.
poles: treat event demand as a growth lane
respect the fixed annual event pool
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: defend the existing event-defended count; add only a differentiated or destination concept that grows or imports the pool, not a generalist share-splitter

conflict_axes.name: easy_low_capital_overbuild_vs_hard_capex_whitespace
conflict_axes.description: The easy near-zero-capital format (thrift) over-builds while the operationally hard capex/skill-gated formats (sign, custom print) stay thin despite demand, the sector's defining asymmetry.
poles: enter the hard capex-gated white space
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: avoid adding to the over-built easy end; pursue the hard white space only with the capex and C-45/skill to clear its barrier

conflict_axes.name: owned_inventory_markdown_vs_landlord_no_inventory
conflict_axes.description: A solo buy-for-resale or vintage shop carries inventory markdown risk, while a multi-dealer antique-mall operator carries none, earning booth rent and commission instead.
poles: own the inventory and the markdown risk
run a landlord-plus-checkout model over micro-inventories
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model the multi-dealer mall as a landlord P&L (booth vacancy risk) distinct from the solo shops' inventory markdown risk

conflict_axes.name: perishable_shrink_vs_durable_aging_stock
conflict_axes.description: The florist's risk is perishable floral shrink on a short cold-chain shelf life, while buy-for-resale formats face durable but aging markdown stock; the cost levers differ.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model the florist on JIT-against-bookings shrink control and the resale formats on tight buying to limit markdown, not one rule for both

edge_cases.description: A stakeholder demands a single actual revenue figure for a named Turlock store
edge_cases.trigger: a question asks the real sales of Vail Creek, Camara's or Main Street Antiques
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the actual-revenue claim; provide only a labeled benchmark estimate with method, public source, confidence and a sales-tax confirmation path

edge_cases.description: Donated-goods thrift high gross margin is read as high profit
edge_cases.trigger: near-zero COGS on a thrift store is mistaken for a fat-margin business
edge_cases.mitigation: load the sector's highest sorting labor and foot-traffic-capped low tickets to show the thin net behind the high gross

edge_cases.description: A sign or custom-print concept is treated as easy white space and budgeted without the C-45 bond and capex
edge_cases.trigger: a demand-headroom read on sign/print omits the $15k bond and the wide-format/screen-press stack
edge_cases.mitigation: run the white space through the capex and C-45 gate before issuing a go; headroom is not easy entry

edge_cases.description: A naive second bridal/formalwear generalist is opened into a fixed annual event pool
edge_cases.trigger: a second store enters on demand depth alone without differentiation or destination strategy
edge_cases.mitigation: default to no-add for a generalist; require a Hispanic-formalwear or destination concept that grows or imports the event pool

edge_cases.description: A 28-dealer antique mall is counted as four competing antiques rivals
edge_cases.trigger: Main Street Antiques is read as four storefronts of head-to-head competition
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the mall as one destination with a landlord P&L, lowering effective antiques competition below the storefront count

edge_cases.description: A gold-buying jeweler operates without precious-metals/secondhand registration
edge_cases.trigger: a jeweler buys gold from the public without police reporting and hold periods
edge_cases.mitigation: register as a secondhand/precious-metals dealer and observe reporting and statutory hold periods before buying from the public

edge_cases.description: A used-bookstore is modeled on a storefront cost base it cannot clear under Amazon leakage
edge_cases.trigger: a physical bookstore pro forma ignores the highest-leakage low-ticket reality that closed Lightly Used Books' store in 2025
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the format as online-leaning; do not assume a storefront occupancy load the low-ticket revenue cannot service

edge_cases.description: A supplier-to-named-business link is upgraded from inference to a stated contract
edge_cases.trigger: an answer asserts a specific florist or sign shop buys from a named distributor without a source
edge_cases.mitigation: keep supplier links labeled representative inference except the documented Vintage Market and Lightly Used Books cases

edge_cases.description: A sixth thrift store is added into an already over-built cluster
edge_cases.trigger: the low-capital, no-license thrift format is entered on its easy entry alone
edge_cases.mitigation: default to no-add for thrift; the cluster is over-built and squeezed by regional and online resale

edge_cases.description: A gift or apparel singleton is read as thin white space ignoring secondary-category straddles and uncatalogued sellers
edge_cases.trigger: a primary-only count reads Gifts as one storefront when secondaries make it ~five
edge_cases.mitigation: fold in secondary categories and treat the 27-count as a floor, not a ceiling, before calling a category thin

edge_cases.description: A mozzarella-style commodity swing — here a gold or stem price spike — outruns a format's margin cushion
edge_cases.trigger: a gold price spike compresses jewelry margin or a stem freight spike raises florist COGS in a season the band averages away
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the benchmark band as wide and low-confidence and re-rate the affected format when an input commodity swings

workflow.action: Size the resident, income and student discretionary floor
workflow.description: State the population, household, income and student figures as cited facts or labeled estimates and flag the fully-discretionary nature
workflow.gate: population, household count, median income and enrollment are stated with the no-payer-buffer caveat

workflow.action: Map the heritage event economy to the formats it sustains
workflow.description: Tie each ancestry share to its anchored event format and durability, with the ~20k Assyrian figure labeled estimate
workflow.gate: all communities have cited or estimate-labeled shares and named anchored formats

workflow.action: Apply the Modesto and online leakage ceiling
workflow.description: Identify which spend leaks to Modesto/Amazon/resale and which formats are exposed
workflow.gate: the leakage channels are named and formats ranked by exposure as a behavioral estimate

workflow.description: Fix the estimate-not-actual label with method + source + confidence, the inference and floor rules
workflow.gate: the label, the cited-fact/inference/floor distinctions and the high-gross-thin-net rule are stated

workflow.description: State COGS/markup/gross by format and net/occupancy/payroll cross-sector ranges with sources
workflow.gate: the COGS/gross/net ranges are stated as cited planning priors with the rent gap flagged

workflow.description: Define benchmark-scaled-down-by-size-signal banding with the estimate label and confirmation path
workflow.gate: every band carries the estimate-not-actual label, a Low-Med confidence, a size signal and a confirmation source

workflow.action: Identify the family-incumbency lever and the supplier map
workflow.description: Explain how family labor and incumbency move the margin and name the realistic supplier universe per format
workflow.gate: the payroll/occupancy suppression and its limits are stated and supplier nodes carry the inference label

workflow.action: Establish the licensing and capex gates
workflow.description: State the seller's-permit floor, the C-45 bond, the secondhand registration and the capex intensity per format
workflow.gate: the cheap seller's-permit floor and the C-45/secondhand/capex gates are stated with sources

workflow.action: Model the four cost spines and the format unit economics
workflow.description: For each spine and format state the dominant cost line, labeled band and the gate or lever that decides viability
workflow.gate: each format names its cost center, labeled band and the gate or lever that decides viability

workflow.action: Model the event-defended and landlord formats
workflow.description: Tie jewelry/bridal/menswear to the fixed event pool and the antique mall to the landlord P&L
workflow.gate: the fixed-event-pool share-splitter logic and the booth-rent landlord P&L are stated

workflow.action: Synthesize the per-format saturation and white space
workflow.description: Give the over-built/differentiated/white-space read with the headroom-is-not-easy-entry and floor-not-ceiling caveats
workflow.gate: each format has a saturation read and the white space is distinguished from the over-built end

workflow.action: Issue the merged format go/no-go verdict
workflow.description: Intersect demand headroom, cost gate and margin reality into an add/avoid call with the constraint-flips-by-category rule
workflow.gate: the verdict states the saturation read, binding cost gate and margin reality and is conditioned on clearing the capex and C-45/secondhand gate

priority_rationale: The discretionary demand floor, heritage event economy and leakage ceiling come first because every format judgment depends on knowing the size and shape of demand; the honesty-labeling discipline, cost-margin backbone, labeled-revenue method, family-incumbency lever and supplier map next, because they are the lenses that turn demand into honestly-labeled unit economics; the seller's-permit floor, C-45 bond, secondhand gate and capex gates next, because they decide enterability independent of demand; the four cost-spine and format models then apply all of that to concrete businesses; and the saturation synthesis and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a defensible add/avoid verdict.

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any revenue claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so a band may never be presented as an actual figure for a named business
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure is attached to a named business or format
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate-not-actual with a method, public source, confidence and confirmation path, and refuse an actual-revenue claim

dominance_rules.rule: The cost gate dominates demand headroom in any entry verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a demand-true white space that cannot clear the C-45 bond, secondhand registration or capex is not enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a go recommendation rests on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: withhold the go until the binding cost gate is shown clearable

dominance_rules.rule: Net margin dominates gross in judging attractiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: high-gross formats (thrift, jewelry, sign) still net thin once labor, sorting, insurance and capex service load
dominance_rules.trigger: a format is judged by its gross or revenue band alone
dominance_rules.action: pair the gross with its net and sorting/labor/capex-service load before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The C-45 bond dominates the sign-install concept decision
dominance_rules.rationale: the $15k bond plus 4-year experience, not substrate cost, decides sign-installation entry
dominance_rules.trigger: a sign-install concept is scoped without confirming the C-45 license
dominance_rules.action: confirm C-45 eligibility and the bond or scope the concept to non-installed signage

dominance_rules.rule: Saturation dominates demand depth for over-built and fixed-pool formats
dominance_rules.rationale: a deep base does not justify adding to an over-built thrift cluster or a fixed-event-pool formalwear count
dominance_rules.trigger: an addition is proposed for thrift, antiques, or a generalist bridal/formalwear store
dominance_rules.action: default to no-add and defend the existing count unless the entrant is differentiated or destination

dominance_rules.rule: Per-format bands dominate any sector average for the typical business
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business figure is public and the bands are deliberately wide and low-confidence
dominance_rules.trigger: a single per-business or sector-average figure is cited as typical
dominance_rules.action: lead with the wide per-format estimate bands and refuse a point figure for a named store

dominance_rules.rule: Documented links dominate inferred supplier links
dominance_rules.rationale: only Vintage Market's Annie Sloan dealership and Lightly Used Books' sourcing are evidenced; the rest is representative inference
dominance_rules.action: label it inference unless it is one of the documented cases

dominance_rules.rule: The landlord P&L dominates the inventory read for a multi-dealer mall
dominance_rules.rationale: a 28-dealer mall earns booth rent and commission and carries no markdown risk, unlike the solo shops
dominance_rules.trigger: a multi-dealer antique mall is modeled or counted as inventory-owning rivals
dominance_rules.action: model it as one landlord-plus-checkout destination, not four inventory-owning competitors

dominance_rules.rule: Coverage is treated as a floor, not a ceiling
dominance_rules.rationale: the 27 catalog count excludes home-based sellers, booth dealers and pop-ups
dominance_rules.trigger: a count or density is cited as a complete figure
dominance_rules.action: label the count and ~3.7/10k density a lower bound and fold in secondary-category straddles

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate-not-actual label with method, source and confidence when the band is first produced, not after review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a revenue figure circulating as a fact for a named business and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run a white space through the capex and C-45/secondhand gate before calling it an opportunity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a demand-true but cost-gated sign/print or precious-metals format and reversing the call

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every gross figure with its net and sorting/labor/capex-service load in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross thrift or jewelry format being approved before the thin net is seen

anti_rework_rules.rule: Default a second event-format store to no-add unless it is differentiated or destination
anti_rework_rules.prevents: opening a generalist bridal/formalwear store that splits a fixed event pool and erodes both

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model the multi-dealer mall as a landlord P&L from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: miscounting a 28-dealer mall as four rivals and mis-modeling its markdown-free economics

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep supplier-to-business links labeled inference except the two documented cases
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inferred supply link hardening into an asserted contract that must later be corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat the 27-count and ~3.7/10k density as a floor and fold in secondaries before a thin-coverage call
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a singleton white-space conclusion that uncatalogued sellers and straddles immediately reverse

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model the used-bookstore and other high-leakage low-ticket formats as online-leaning, not storefront
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a physical-store pro forma failing on an occupancy load the low-ticket revenue cannot clear

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA or Turlock Finance sales-tax data becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled revenue bands with confirmed figures and re-rank confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Census ACS refresh changes population, income or ancestry shares
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the discretionary floor and re-map the heritage anchors and saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a commodity or input swing (gold, diamonds, floral freight, substrate, blank garments) lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the affected format cost centers and the cost-margin and supply-chain nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a CSLB C-45 bond/requirement or a secondhand/precious-metals rule changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the sign-install and gold-buying entry gates and the affected verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format opens or closes, changing a per-format count
iteration_protocol.action: update the saturation read and the merged go/no-go for that format

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cross-shop leakage study or measured Modesto/online-capture figure is produced
iteration_protocol.action: replace the behavioral leakage estimate and re-rank the exposed formats

iteration_protocol.trigger: the catalog floor is expanded with newly found independents or secondary-category recounts
iteration_protocol.action: update the coverage-floor density and re-rate any thin white-space reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: equipment or financing costs for the capex-gated formats change
iteration_protocol.action: update the capex intensity and the substrate-conversion entry verdict
